judgment_text: The Court laid down comprehensive guidelines for arrest and bail. It categorized offences into A, B, C, D categories. Held that bail is the rule and jail is the exception. Strict compliance with Section 41 and 41A CrPC mandated. For offenses punishable with 7 years or less, arrest only if conditions in Section 41(1)(b) satisfied.
sections_cited: CrPC 41, CrPC 41A, CrPC 88, CrPC 170, CrPC 436, CrPC 437, CrPC 439

case_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
judgment_text: Landmark judgment on Section 498A IPC and Section 41 CrPC. Police cannot automatically arrest in cases with punishment up to 7 years. Must issue Notice of Appearance under Section 41A CrPC. Magistrate must not authorize detention mechanically without perusing police report recording reasons for arrest.

case_title: Sanjay Chandra v. CBI (2G Spectrum Case)
judgment_text: The Court emphasized that the object of bail is to secure the appearance of the accused at trial. Seriousness of the charge is not the only factor. Pre-trial detention has punitive consequences. Economic offences are not to be treated as a distinct class for denying bail.

case_title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab
judgment_text: Constitution Bench judgment on Anticipatory Bail (Section 438 CrPC). Held that the power is of wide amplitude and should not be hemmed in by restrictions not found in the statute. Anticipatory bail is not limited to a fixed period.

case_title: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi)
judgment_text: Reaffirmed Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia. Held that anticipatory bail need not be time-bound and can continue till the end of the trial. Limits on anticipatory bail should be imposed only in special circumstances.

case_title: P. Chidambaram v. Directorate of Enforcement
judgment_text: Granted bail in PMLA case. Held that even in economic offences, bail is the rule. Gravity of offence is a factor but not the sole ground to deny bail. Triple test (flight risk, tampering, influencing witnesses) satisfied.

case_title: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India
judgment_text: Upheld the constitutionality of PMLA Section 45 twin conditions. Held that stringent bail conditions in special statutes like PMLA are not unconstitutional given the object of check money laundering.

case_title: Tofan Singh v. State of Tamil Nadu
judgment_text: Held that officers of Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) are police officers and confessions made to them under Section 67 NDPS Act are inadmissible in evidence.

case_title: Rhea Chakraborty v. Union of India (Bombay HC)
judgment_text: Granted bail in NDPS case. Held that Section 27A (financing illicit traffic) was not applicable. Mere payment for drugs for consumption does not amount to financing illicit traffic.
Denied bail in Excise Policy case. Observed that a prima facie case was made out. However, directed trial to be completed in 6-8 months, else liberty to apply for bail again.

case_title: Moti Ram v. State of Madhya Pradesh
judgment_text: Justice Krishna Iyer famously stated 'Bail not Jail'. Criticized the demand for excessive surety amounts from indigent accused, calling it a denial of bail.
Held that delay in concluding the trial is a valid ground for granting bail, even in serious offences involving UAPA/terrorism charges.

case_title: Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb
judgment_text: Held that statutory restrictions on bail (like UAPA Section 43D(5)) do not oust the Constitutional Court's power to grant bail on grounds of violation of Article 21 (Speedy Trial) if there is prolonged incarceration without trial.
Elaborated on the philosophy of bail. Personal liberty is too precious to be squandered. Bail conditions must be reasonable, not elusive.

case_title: Dataram Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
judgment_text: Emphasized humane approach to bail. A person is innocent until proven guilty. Prolonged imprisonment without trial is punitive.
